title: Seven sailors missing after Black Sea drone strikes

slides.headline: Seven sailors missing after Black Sea drone strikes
slides.subtitle: Two commercial tankers were hit near Romania's coast.

slides.explanation: Seven people are missing after the attacks. This is roughly the size of a small crew on a fishing boat suddenly lost at sea.

slides.headline: A NATO source identifies Russia as the culprit
slides.explanation: While the attacks happened near Romania, a NATO source directly attributed the drones to Russia. This moves the conflict closer to NATO territory.
We compared reports from six independent outlets including the BBC and Al Jazeera. All agree on the core facts of the incident.

slides.subtitle: Read the full breakdown on Headlinne.

caption:
A concerning turn of events in the Black Sea.

Two commercial tankers were struck by drones near the Romanian coast, leaving seven sailors missing and the ships on fire.

Romania's president has called the attack unacceptable. While the exact circumstances are still being investigated, a NATO source has pointed to Russia as the origin of the drones.

This incident highlights how quickly the regional conflict can spill over into vital shipping lanes. It raises major security questions for commercial vessels operating in the area.

story.title: Seven sailors missing after drones strike tankers near Romania’s Black Sea coast
story.summary: Nato source says drones came from Russia, while Romania’s president says attacking commercial ships ‘is unacceptable and has to stop’ Seven sailors are missing after drones struck two tankers near Romania’s Black Sea ⁠coast, setting them ablaze and raising ⁠fresh security concerns on a ​vital shipping route used by Ukraine. A Nato military source told Reuters the drones that had hit the Wine Trader and the Yara J came from Russia. “The drones that caused ⁠the fires on board two tankers inside Romanian territorial waters were of Russian origin,” the source said.
